description: Revocation closure `retraction-after-correction` over the 28-entry toy corpus (core spec §5.1, §5.3), evaluated at the checkpoint committing the trigger.
note: Record A was corrected twice earlier in the corpus — to A2 at entry 6 and to A3 (hmac-sha256:72f6f4c6c0a09ac7610d6ce218218c3e8623a8b2bb502f41821d99af2ab82670) at entry 12 — and is now RETRACTED outright at entry 18. Core spec §5.1: "For a retraction on (ds, X), the seed set is exactly {(ds, X)} — retractions never seed superseded replacements." So the seeds are {A} alone, and the consumers of A2 — S1' (sha256:8465148cf16c5b91c0e6001f3e3a985ae456890500745f5893a60c0692bb1d7c) at entry 7 and W1/W2 at entry 10 — are NOT affected. Retracting A says nothing about A2: A2 is a separately introduced record with its own history. Contrast `supersession-chain`, where a *correction* of the same original does seed A2, because that correction supersedes the one that produced it.
